title: Found Unconscious
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a young woman found unconscious with respiratory depression, hypotension, and altered mental status. ECG shows widened QRS, prolonged QT — classic TCA cardiotoxicity. The 'Three C's' of TCA poisoning: Coma, Convulsions, Cardiac arrhythmias. Management priorities: ABCs — intubate for airway protection (GCS depressed), mechanical ventilation. IV fluids for hypotension (TCA blocks alpha-1 receptors → vasodilation). Sodium bicarbonate for cardiac toxicity (QRS >100ms or ventricular arrhythmia) — alkalinization to pH 7.45-7.55 favors non-ionized TCA, reducing sodium channel blockade. Activated charcoal via NG tube if within 2 hours of ingestion (airway must be secured first). 'Coma cocktail': check glucose, give thiamine before D50. Naloxone for possible opioid co-ingestion. CT head to rule out trauma (unwitnessed). Aspirin and acetaminophen levels for common co-ingestants. Psychiatry consult after stabilization for suicide attempt.
chief_complaint: Found unconscious, respiratory depression, suspected overdose

stacks.finding: Screening.

stacks.finding: Unwitnessed — rule out head trauma causing obtundation.

stacks.label: CPK, serum
stacks.finding: Unknown down time — rhabdomyolysis risk. Prevent AKI.

stacks.label: HCG, beta (pregnancy test)
stacks.finding: Child-bearing woman — pregnancy test before radiation. Ectopic can cause this presentation.

stacks.finding: Screening labs.

stacks.label: Toxicology screen, urine / serum
stacks.finding: Drug screen in any overdose.

stacks.label: Ethanol / Toxic alcohol panel
stacks.finding: History suggests ethanol abuse — common co-ingestant.

stacks.label: Salicylate level
stacks.finding: Aspirin is common co-ingestant in overdose.

stacks.label: TCA level, serum
stacks.finding: Urine/serum positive for TCA — quantify level.

stacks.label: Oxygen
stacks.finding: Low SpO2 — supplemental O2 before intubation.

stacks.label: Thiamine (Vitamin B1)
stacks.finding: Coma cocktail — thiamine before D50 to prevent Wernicke-Korsakoff.

stacks.label: Dextrose 50%
stacks.finding: Coma cocktail — if hypoglycemic. Give thiamine first.

stacks.label: Naloxone
stacks.finding: Give in any overdose to rule out reversible opioid overdose.

stacks.label: IV fluids (NS / LR)
stacks.finding: TCA overdose → hypotension from alpha-1 blockade. IV fluids for BP.

stacks.label: Nasogastric tube with suction
stacks.finding: Prevent aspiration (intubated). Required for GI decontamination and activated charcoal.

stacks.label: Activated charcoal
stacks.finding: GI decontamination if within 2 hours of ingestion. Only after airway secured. Via NG tube.

stacks.label: Intubation, endotracheal
stacks.finding: Respiratory depression — airway protection required.

stacks.label: Mechanical ventilation
stacks.finding: Respiratory depression — ventilatory support.

stacks.label: Sodium bicarbonate
stacks.finding: For TCA cardiac toxicity (QRS >100ms, ventricular arrhythmia). Alkalinize to pH 7.45-7.55. Increases extracellular Na+ and favors non-ionized TCA.

stacks.label: Consult, psychiatry
stacks.finding: Potential suicide attempt — psychiatry consult after medical stabilization.

stacks.label: IV access
stacks.finding: Good practice for IV fluids/meds.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Widened QRS, prolonged QT on ECG. Tachycardia (anticholinergic). Hypotension (alpha-1 blockade).
physical_exam.respiratory: Depressed — requires intubation and mechanical ventilation.
physical_exam.neurological: Obtunded, GCS depressed. Coma — one of the 'Three C's'.
physical_exam.psychiatric: Suicide attempt — psychiatry consult after stabilization.

decoys.label: Activated charcoal WITHOUT securing airway
decoys.reason_wrong: NEVER give charcoal without secure airway (ETT). Risk of aspiration pneumonitis. Intubate first, then charcoal via NG.

decoys.label: Flumazenil
decoys.reason_wrong: Flumazenil is contraindicated in overdose of unknown etiology — can precipitate seizures, especially with TCA co-ingestion.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Respiratory depression = secure airway. TCA overdose = coma, convulsions, cardiac toxicity ('Three C's').
Widened QRS (>100ms) = sodium channel blockade. Bicarb to pH 7.45-7.55: favors non-ionized TCA, less Na+ channel binding.
Activated charcoal via NG tube if <2 hours since ingestion. Airway must be secured first.
After medical stabilization. Determine disposition — may need psychiatric inpatient admission.

case_summary: TCA overdose (suicide attempt). Obtunded + widened QRS + hypotension. Intubate → bicarb → charcoal → ICU. Psych consult after stabilization.
